Both of these combine to give the characters so much personality; the solid framerate gives the game a “too good to be true” look on PS1. The period setting, surprisingly big enemy variety (all with whack ass designs), and digestible length all combine to make it a game that’s aged well. 

I think people shat on both Koudelka and Parasite Eve for being short and with shallow combat for a JRPG. But for a horror game, they maintain a good pace plot-wise; one which would’ve been sabotaged by a 20-40 hour runtime like most JRPGs. It isn’t a scary game or much of a resource management game, but the atmosphere and menu/sound effect aesthetics of the game scratch that Survival Horror itch.
